COMPUTER SCIENCE / WORKING METHOD

A learning plan should eventually produce something other than a learning plan.

Nandini Thakur · 2 min read

I enjoy a well-organised roadmap. Possibly enough to need a roadmap for when to stop organising it.

My own approach is to connect learning to something I can explain, reproduce, or build. Reading gives me a first pass. Trying to use the idea tells me where that first pass was a little optimistic.

A smaller definition of progress

For a concept, I want a short explanation in my own words and a worked example I can reproduce. For a system, I want to understand the inputs, the failure modes, and the decisions behind the design. For a project, I want a functioning artifact and a readable explanation of its limits.

Stay with the difficult sentence

“I understand it, I just can’t explain it” is a sentence I’m trying to become more suspicious of. Sometimes the vocabulary is missing. Sometimes the understanding is. Either way, writing it down gives me something specific to work on.

This section is where I’ll work through computer science, data engineering, and the systems behind financial applications. Some notes will be small. I would rather a small idea be clear than a large one be decorated.

Keep the loop short

Learn a thing. Try a thing. Write down what broke. Revisit the explanation. That is the loop I want to get better at. The beautifully formatted tracker is allowed to watch.

Still thinking this through. A good counterargument is welcome.

I have opinions. I’m also quite happy to revise them.
